action.question: How should I handle the .idea/ directory?

questions.question: How should I handle the .idea/ directory?

options.label: Untrack all of .idea/ + add to .gitignore (Recommended)
options.description: Remove the entire `.idea/` directory from git tracking and add `.idea/` to .gitignore. Matches the convention for most public Java/Maven repos; future IntelliJ users keep their own settings. Cleanest. Local working copy unaffected.

options.label: Just remove the docker runConfigurations file
options.description: Delete only `.idea/runConfigurations/dstrader_docker_Dockerfile.xml` (the file with the cross-repo sourceFilePath). Keep codeStyles/compiler.xml/etc. tracked. Minimal change, preserves any code-style/inspection settings you've curated for collaborators.

options.label: Keep all of .idea/ — just leave the cross-repo file as-is
options.description: Accept the existing situation. Anyone cloning + opening in IntelliJ sees a broken Dockerfile run-config they have to fix, but it's not a security/leak concern.

questions.question: Heads-up: the human-review 24h pause restarts after we change source. OK?

options.label: OK — restart the 24h after the fixes land
options.description: Standard SOP behavior. After README + .idea/ fix lands on dstrader, we re-rewrite to dstrader-r2 and re-run SOP; the new human-diff.patch starts a fresh 24h window. Earliest Phase 3 push slips ~24h from when the new audit completes.

options.label: Skip the pause restart — the delta is trivial
options.description: Treat the 1-line README change + .idea/ removal as too small to warrant a full 24h pause restart. Owner accepts the residual risk that the small delta might hide something. Faster path to Phase 3.
